finding: DE-B02: original fund-exit positive-gain and dated holding gates no longer explicit in current abbreviated routing paragraph or named companion
current_exact_wording: - **Exit tax.** A client fully liable for at least seven of the last twelve years who holds § 17 shares faces a deemed sale on moving abroad, or on giving the shares to someone not liable in Germany ([§ 6 AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__6.html)). Payment can be spread over seven yearly instalments on application; there is no open-ended EU/EEA deferral for triggers from 2022, and the tax falls away on return within seven years if conditions are met. Fund units are caught at 1% of a fund or a cost of EUR 500,000 ([§ 19(3) InvStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/invstg_2018/__19.html)). Full detail: leaving-germany-exit-tax.
old_exact_wording: - **Fund units** are also caught if the client held at least 1% of a fund's issued units at any time in the last five years, or at the time of the trigger holds units in the fund that cost at least EUR 500,000 ([§ 19(3) InvStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/invstg_2018/__19.html): "mindestens 500 000 Euro"). Either test only applies if the client's taxable gains on the fund units are positive overall ("insgesamt positiv"). The deemed gain is flat-tax income with the fund's tax-free share.

options.A_recommended: Replace the fund-units sentence only: "For private fund units, §19(3) applies only if the aggregate taxable gains calculated under §19(1), §22 and §56 are positive overall and the investor either held at least 1% of the fund’s issued units at some point in the preceding five years or holds units in that fund costing at least EUR 500,000 at the trigger date."
options.B: Keep the short threshold sentence but immediately add: "The 1% test looks back five years; the EUR 500,000 cost test is measured at the trigger. Both require positive aggregate taxable gains under §19(3)."

separating_control: A1% holding sold down below1% before departure can still meet the five-year test; a €500000 holding with overall zero taxable gain fails the positive-gain condition. No negative deemed loss is supplied.
